selection_policy.purpose: Convert the first Research Queue batch from generic missing-research status into evidence-backed next-research priority without changing Candidate membership.
selection_policy.portfolio_context: Prefer cross-style information gain and avoid concentrating first-pass research in resource-cycle names while the Real account already has high JOVO Energy concentration.

research_objects.variant_wedge: Low valuation, large cash balance and high cash distribution create defensive optionality while publishing/distribution core profit is steadier than headline revenue.
research_objects.first_rejection: If normalized earnings depend mainly on tax-policy benefits or receivables/inventory consume cash without operating improvement, the apparent value case weakens materially.
d2_questions: Normalize 2024-2026 earnings for tax-policy effects and non-core income.
Explain working-capital seasonality, receivables and inventory conversion.
Quantify sustainable dividend capacity and capital-allocation discipline.
Separate publishing/distribution economics from low-margin ancillary businesses.
Define valuation and fundamental invalidation bands.

research_objects.variant_wedge: Current earnings recovery is visible and valuation is moderate, but the key research question is how much of the uplift is hydrology normalization versus a durable cash-flow improvement.
research_objects.first_rejection: If normalized-water earnings, leverage and financing costs imply materially lower through-cycle free cash flow than the current run-rate suggests, do not advance beyond research.
d2_questions: Normalize generation and profit across dry/normal/wet hydrology years.
Rebuild debt, financing-cost and maturity profile.
Quantify dividend capacity under normalized hydrology.
Compare valuation and cash yield with 长江电力 and utility alternatives.
Define water-level, leverage and valuation invalidation triggers.

latest_financial_evidence.comparison_note: Prior-year comparison was restated for the 2025 same-control acquisition of the Hulunbuir testing subsidiary.

research_objects.variant_wedge: Testing-infrastructure economics may compound with industry testing complexity, but the current research case depends on proving returns on the large new capital program rather than simply extrapolating reported growth.
research_objects.first_rejection: If new testing capacity produces weak utilization/ROIC or acquisition-driven growth masks weak organic growth, the valuation premium is not justified.
d2_questions: Separate organic growth from acquisition/consolidation effects.
Model utilization, pricing, incremental margins and ROIC for new testing capacity.
Assess convertible-bond dilution and balance-sheet implications.
Map competitive moat and customer concentration.
Define valuation ceiling and utilization/ROIC kill conditions.

research_objects.variant_wedge: The operating pipeline is growing, but headline profit growth overstates underlying earnings quality because settlement-related nonrecurring gains are material.
research_objects.first_rejection: If normalized game economics, user acquisition payback or product concentration cannot support the current expectations embedded in valuation, keep it out of D2 priority.
d2_questions: Normalize 2026 earnings excluding arbitration/settlement and other nonrecurring items.
Build title-level revenue, lifecycle and concentration map.
Assess IP/legal residual risk and cash conversion.
Test valuation against normalized earnings rather than reported headline profit.
Require evidence of durable pipeline economics before D2 promotion.

research_objects.variant_wedge: Integrated coal-power scale and visible capacity additions can support earnings, but the research priority is reduced by commodity/power-cycle overlap with the Real account's existing energy concentration.
research_objects.first_rejection: If normalized coal spreads, tariffs, capex and leverage do not offer sufficient compensation versus less-correlated alternatives, do not allocate scarce D2 research capacity here first.
d2_questions: Normalize coal-price and power-tariff sensitivity across cycles.
Model capex, commissioning and debt trajectory for projects under construction.
Quantify free-cash-flow/dividend capacity after expansion spending.
Measure portfolio-factor overlap with existing energy exposure.
Define valuation discount required to compensate for cyclicality and overlap.
